questions.answer: No. No agents or troops start on the map. Each country starts with its marked city corrupted and its marked station corrupted with a botnet; each pool holds one round of agent income, which lands in the opening adversary turn (like SI's initial Explore).
6: base 5 plus 1 from the economy space uncovered by the setup node (plus nothing from cards yet).
questions.unsure: Whether Round start runs in round 1, since the game 'starts with the adversary's turn'

questions.answer: Before: step B (adversary turn) precedes step D (action phase) every round. No Fast/Slow; all players act at once in D, and what you set up meets next round's adversary turn.

The country's whole pool splits evenly over every site of type X in that country, any owner. The remainder goes one each to the lowest-numbered such sites that aren't the adversary's or firewalled; if too few, then to the adversary's. A firewalled site's share stays in the supply.
questions.unsure: What happens if the country has no site of type X

questions.answer: The book has no 'Deploy' line; reading it as Muster: each troop lands on the country's lowest-numbered factory (any owner), else lowest-numbered city. If the Protector's node is on that hex (Wall), the troop stays in the supply and nothing moves on to the next site.
questions.unsure: The term Deploy is not in the book

questions.answer: No. A troop doesn't damage where it stands. Each of its 2 steps: remove an ambassador on its hex, else strike a player-owned research station or factory on or next to it (then it leaves the map), else move toward the nearest such target. It can hit only player-owned stations and factories, never nodes, cities, or neutral/adversary facilities.
Its first step removes one ambassador there (players choose whose). Its second step removes another if one remains, otherwise strikes or moves as usual.
No. A node hex needs 2 agents; with 1 the node survives (unless the hex's own site hits its corrupt number, impossible with 1).

Every agent next to a hex with a player's node moves onto it (players choose if next to several); a hex then holding 2 agents loses its node (protections apply, marker left) and the agents go to supply. Not on a firewalled hex.

No. The printed number is energy you pay. Placing costs the power or card's cost plus the space's energy; a free-placement card pays neither. What the uncovered space shows (income, dispatch, tag, capstone) is what you gain.
Once a round in the action phase: pay 1 energy plus the uncovered track space's energy to place a node on a land hex in reach with no node, no corruption marker and no land corruption.
Protector rule: when an adversary troop ends its march next to one of your nodes, gain 1 insight, spendable this round. Once per troop per march; a troop used up striking doesn't pay.
questions.unsure: What 'in any march' covers, and whether a troop that couldn't move counts as ending its march

questions.answer: In step 6 of each adversary turn, in each country with a Protector node, 1 troop lands on that country's lowest-numbered adversary or neutral factory (never a player's, never a city). With none, none lands. If Wall blocks that hex, it stays in the supply.
No. Shelter lasts from the action phase to cleanup: production, threats, war, never the adversary's turn.

Each converted agent becomes your ambassador on the hex where it stood (agents on or next to a city in reach). Agents come off first, then ambassadors go on; an agent left on that hex trades 1:1 with one.

Agents landing in that country from a Rally or card line; troops still land and Gather/Push still move agents in. Until the end of the next adversary turn (step 12); the pool then lands at the first Rally after, with income added.
Yes: a Corrupt prohibition also stops natural corruption on sites where its condition holds, and no agent moves onto them.
questions.unsure: Whether it also covers the node-hex half of natural corruption

questions.answer: Muster N: N adversary troops land in each country one at a time on its lowest-numbered factory (any owner); with none, its lowest-numbered city; with none, none. +1 troop per Muster from level 2. Wall and Muster prohibitions block (troop stays in supply).
The side's tip count including this tip: strength I on tips 1-2, II on 3-5, III from tip 6.
No. Unity put against Discord removes Discord; only the rest goes on the Unity track.
You survive 6 Discord tips and lose on the 7th. Yes, the overflow (2) stays on the track toward the next tip.

Any player with a node or ambassador on or next to one of its tokens may pay (resources pooled; a tag payment by one player alone). Target is the player whose node is closest to a token at any distance; tied players choose.
No. Tag items never change with level; only resource items get surcharges.
5 ambassadors from your supply (factory 3 + 1 per agent); the 2 agents are removed and the factory becomes yours.
questions.unsure: The price's unit (ambassadors) is only implied by 'Who pays'

questions.answer: Once a round per player, after its megaproject completes, if any city of that megacorp's country (corrupted ones too) is in your reach.

At a Discord tip: your ambassador on that base stops the drone it would get (and is spent); one on the neutral factory stops one of its drones; an agent on the neutral factory stops all its drones; a full base takes none. Owning the factory (not neutral) also stops it. Warmongering/project drones have no stopper. In war, protect the struck factory instead.
questions.unsure: Which base goes without when a factory ambassador stops one; no way named to remove a drone already at a base

questions.answer: No. Only your own ambassador on the hex can be spent as protection. A teammate's ambassador can still cancel arriving agents 1:1, which helps indirectly.
Yes. At 6+ Unity tips the purge asks only for no corrupted cities; stations and land don't count. You win at the next check unless a loss triggers at the same time.

gaps: Where does a Rally pool go if its country has no site of the named type: does it stay in the pool or go back to supply?

overall: The hardest part was the adversary turn: twelve steps, three ways agents converge or corrupt, and two near-identical corruption events with opposite marker rules. My Spirit Island habits mostly misfired on order (Rally lands and corrupts the same turn; the adversary goes before you; there is no Fast window) and on troops, which strike adjacent facilities and vanish instead of ravaging their land. The book defuses the biggest trap well by saying outright that track numbers are costs and the card-play track is not a play limit. Tell the designer: make the Claim price's unit (ambassadors) explicit in the table, rename either the Protector's Wall or the Wall icon, and fix the legend's stray Alignment track and income track. It felt like about 45 minutes of reading, plus one look-up per round for a while.
